A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete main text, references, and Appendices A–K. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support a reliable comparison of all 25 pages.

before.justification: v3 reports original MEMENTO experiments on TSP and CVRP in Section 4, with additional benchmarks, ablations, and sensitivity analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark comparisons and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The memory storage and retrieval procedure, MLP-based logit corrections, training objective, and inference procedure in Section 3 and Appendix B are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same TSP/CVRP benchmarks, generalization datasets, 500-node evaluations, augmentation scenarios, and instance-size scaling tests.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding tables, including POMO, EAS/EAS-Emb, SGBS, COMPASS, and the listed classical and large-instance solvers.

E3.justification: Dataset sizes, metrics, checkpoints, search budgets, augmentation procedures, and timing protocols are unchanged. Both retain the standard 1,600-attempt evaluation and the same larger-instance and runtime-budget settings.

E4.justification: The scaling and batch-budget studies, input-feature ablations, training curves, learned-update analyses, and training-budget sensitivity results are retained unchanged, including Appendices G–K.

E5.justification: Figure 5's standard-deviation reporting and the graphical reporting practices are unchanged. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or statistical-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Reported numbers, rankings, curves, and findings match throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 1 retains MEMENTO's TSP100 objective/gap of 7.768/0.045% and CVRP100 objective/gap of 15.657/0.066%.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Section 3, training-loss reasoning in Appendix B, and derivation connecting MEMENTO to REINFORCE in Appendix F are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about memory-based adaptation, zero-shot combination with COMPASS, and scalability, including the claim of state-of-the-art performance on 11 of 12 tasks.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including budget-dependent exploration, regimes where EAS performs better, computational and memory overheads, runtime-comparison caveats, and the training-budget tuning bias.

D1.justification: Implementation, hardware, hyperparameters, checkpoint descriptions, and code/data access information are unchanged. The code-availability footnote changes from 2 to 1, but its wording and destination remain identical.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to construction methods, diversity-based solvers, and inference-time policy adaptation.

P1.justification: v4 adds an equal-contribution marker to Refiloe Shabe and revises the first-page note to credit equal contribution with Felix Chalumeau. It also updates the version/date stamp and renumbers the code footnote. Body and appendix wording and structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions, and their placement remain unchanged, including the appendices. The author-note, footnote-marker, and version-stamp text edits do not reorganize the page layout.

improvement.justification: v4 clarifies author credit and renumbers a footnote, while preserving the scientific exposition, experimental evidence, analyses, limitations, and reproducibility information. These limited administrative edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
